title: Bangladesh forms wage board as garment protests turn violent
paragraphs: DHAKA: Bangladesh announced a six-member wage board on Sunday (Nov 1) to review garment workers' pay and urged employees to return to work, but protests demanding higher wages continued across major industrial areas, disrupting transport and factory operations.

Workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (U$245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.

The dispute has raised concerns about disruption to an industry that employs about 4 million workers, generates more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh's export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western brands.
